card.title: 211th TOKYO
card.flavorText: The 211th Infantry Regiment was part of the Imperial Japanese Army's 32nd Division, which was formed in April 1939. Initially based in Kyoto, the division was organized as a standard triangular infantry division and drew many of its troops from the Kansai region. The 32nd Division was first deployed to China during the Second Sino-Japanese War. There, it served under the 11th Army and participated in the Battle of Zaoyang-Yichang in 1940. After returning to Japan, the division was later sent to the Pacific theater as the war expanded. In 1944, it was assigned to the defense of the Philippines, particularly on the island of Leyte. There, it became part of the Japanese 35th Army. During the Battle of Leyte, the 32nd Division was heavily engaged and suffered devastating losses while attempting to resist the American landings. Cut off and outnumbered, it was gradually destroyed in the mountainous heart of the island. Disease, hunger, and lack of supplies took a greater toll than combat. Very few soldiers of the division survived the campaign. The 32nd Division's experience in Leyte was typical of many Japanese units late in the war: isolated, under-supplied, and ordered to fight to the end. Its destruction marked one of many costly defeats for Japan in the Philippines.
